persons.name: Marianne
persons.note: CARDED FROM THE BORDERLINE ROSTER'S R6 (T-1504, stage `underdocumented`, sub-stage `church_register`). Named in St Mary's baptismal register at Chicago in 1833, with the priest's own word for an Indigenous woman written onto her name and onto no other name on the line. No 1835 corroboration and no card. The licence is R3's — a dated appearance inside the window, priced against the persistence model — and the husband and the children named on the same entries the town already carries. The register prints her as `Marianne (sauvage)`, in the mother's place of entry 14 of 1833, at `Chicago, Cook County, Illinois`, in the hand of J. M. I. Saint Cyr, dated 1833-10. NO SURNAME IS INVENTED: the book gives her a forename and the priest's parenthesis and nothing else, and her husband's surname is his. A baptism documents a person at a font on a day. It is not a residence, an address, an occupation or an arrival, and this card asserts none of them. What the dated appearance bounds is that she was at Chicago on that day; what it does not bound is where she slept, whose roof it was, or whether she was still here on 1 July 1835 — that last is what the persistence draw prices and says out loud. The research READ this row and left it `unresolved`, handing the kinship on to T-1335; that ruling is not overturned, and this record is a reconstruction of what the town looks like if the name is admitted at the limit of its own evidence. The reading, the source and the ruling stand at `church:data/research/church/records/st_marys_baptisms_1833_1835.json#records/st_marys_bapt_1833_14_3_mother#0` in data/reconstruction/1835_borderline_roster.json. REVIEW REQUIRED: this card is a record of a Native woman at Chicago in the three years of the removal, and AGENTS.md's standing constraint holds it for review by Native scholars or community organisations before any scene carrying it may be marked released. No figure is drawn (L1).

TWO OF THIS FAMILY'S NAMED VARIANTS ARE REFUSED AND TWO STAND (T-1686): the hip its roof line offers ("side gable or hip, 6:12-9:12") is refused rather than quietly substituted, because a hip, gambrel or mansard roof on a Chicago house in 1835 would be a claim and not a default; the Greek doorway its variants name is refused BY DATE — the earliest Greek Revival house in Chicago is the Clarke House of 1836, which data/exclusions.json keeps out of this scene, so no entablature, corner pilaster or portico stands on a roof of 1835-07-01; and the corner boards and the one-to-two chimneys the same line names already stand: the trim follows the stud module the construction argument picks.
